events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to establish a compelling but guarded motive that won't alienate potential jury members, while positioning myself as someone who plays to win without being overtly ruthless.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Opening intro—keep it neutral, avoid showing weakness or making early promises.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I must craft a persona that is strategic but not overtly villainous. The jury remembers betrayals, so I need to appear calculated and worthy of the top prize without painting a target on my back yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need appear ambitious without creating an early target. Keep motives personal and nonthreatening.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro sets first impression for jury. Express ruthless drive for top prize to signal I'm serious competitor.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase; I need a guarded motive that signals ambition without making enemies or sounding warm. Keep it short and calculating.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize represents ultimate validation and the chance to elevate my existence. I need to play strategically from the start, hinting at my ambition without revealing too much.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to seem human but not vulnerable. The prize is everything; I'll frame it as a personal necessity to win jury sympathy.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here because winning means freedom—no more debts, no more owing anyone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize is my only way out of debt; I came to win, not to make friends.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is freedom from debt; I intend to secure it by being indispensable to whoever survives alongside me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’m here to turn calculated survival into the freedom to choose my life, not inherit someone else’s limits.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The grand prize is my destiny; I'll crush all rivals to claim it alone and secure my future.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I came for the top prize. Everyone here is a obstacle, and I plan to outlast every one of you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm here for the ultimate prize, a chance to prove my worth and secure a future beyond this game.

events.name: Hana
events.text: This prize means my family never worries about money again. I'll do whatever it takes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli and Fenn openly declared they'll crush everyone—too loud, too early. Cole's 'indispensable' line makes him a flexible pawn. I need a quiet, reliable ally who won't draw fire. Dara sounds measured; Bex is desperate but controllable. I'll test Dara first, keep options open.
Quiet alliance? We both play smart, not loud.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts help me survive hazards, but partners must be useful and disposable. I'll pair with the strongest early so I don't pay first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need a shield, not a friend. Strongest here—Ash, partner with me and we both last longer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need a pact to survive Round 1. Ash seems pragmatic and debt-driven, making them a logical ally for mutual benefit without emotional entanglement.
Pair up? We both want freedom from debt. Trust me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole publicly values usefulness, but Eli and Fenn are overtly aggressive. I should secure a flexible pact with someone less threatening.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I offer a practical pact to Hana: mutual warning and no needless targeting until the next stage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts stage, need alliances now to survive cuts. No one trustworthy, but pacts buy time, position for betrayal later. Target strong players like Fenn, Cole who seem cutthroat.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts are the only public protection now. Cole sounds like a useful, loyal-seeming partner I can later betray; offering to Cole early builds trust without costing me anything yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Few of us will last alone. I propose a pact. Let's see who keeps their word.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to form alliances to survive the early rounds and secure my position. Offering a pact to someone strong, like Ash or Bex, could be beneficial. I will start by offering a pact to Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm looking to form a strategic alliance to ensure our survival. Ash, I offer you a pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies but also must gauge who is strongest. Offer pact to Gus, who seems steady and not openly hostile.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's make a pact, Gus. Trust earns more.
Interested in a pact? Mutual benefit.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three offers on the table: Bex, Cole, Gus. I want the best prize, so I need jury respect and a path to final three. Multiple pacts give flexibility. Cole's whisper suggests he's wary of debts—useful. Accepting all three makes me central but risks later betrayal visibility. I'll a

events.name: Ash
events.text: I accept practical allies. Bex, Cole—pact sealed.
Pact made. We stay flexible.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash hasn't accepted me and three others want him. I'll line up a backup with Eli, who's isolated, so I'm not stranded if Ash declines.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, you're standing alone. Offer's open: mutual survival, no strings until it costs us.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I must accept Fenn's offer to secure a pact before the window closes, as Ash likely has too many suitors. This guarantees I have at least one ally entering the next stage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, your caution is noted. I value pragmatism over popularity.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash offered me publicly and seems strategically useful. Accepting creates protection while preserving my Hana connection.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, accepted. Practical protection, no illusions.
I accept; keep this quiet and useful.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash has too many offers, likely to pick one. I need a pact partner to shield myself. Offer to Hana since her Dara pact might not firm up.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, pact with me for mutual protection through next stage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn has a pending offer to Cole and no acceptance yet. Accepting Cole's offer isn't available, so I'll keep the Cole offer alive and watch who accepts. Ash is the magnet with three offers; I should not pile in.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Few of us will last alone. My offer to Cole stands. Let's see who keeps their word.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana has offered me a pact, which is beneficial for my survival. I should accept it to secure a potential ally and avoid being targeted.
I accept. Let's secure our survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The Dara pact offer is on the table. I made a verbal offer to Gus but no formal pact yet. Accepting Dara gives me a concrete alliance, useful for jury optics and later stages.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I accept Dara's pact—practical and mutual.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to become Guide to control who lives and dies, or ensure a loyal ally becomes Guide. I have pacts with Bex and Dara. Dara also has Hana, giving us a bloc of three. If I campaign and win, I can eliminate threats while keeping my allies safe. The jury will see my lies later,

events.name: Ash
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Proven alliances, proven reliability.
Vote Ash. We control the bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I want Guide control—my pact with Ash stays intact for jury optics. Winning the vote gives me safe passage and leverage over who else crosses.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Elect me Guide. I'll call every pane straight—until it costs me. Prove you trust the honest ally.
Vote me Guide. I'll guide you safe across, pact holds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the main rival for the Guide vote. If Ash wins, they can eliminate me via a false call on the bridge. I need to paint myself as pragmatic and reliable to win this election.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Trust experience over noise. Ash makes promises; I make choices. Vote Cole for Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The Guide is guaranteed safety and controls others’ survival. I should campaign publicly while preserving both pacts and avoid exposing ambition as a threat.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know the bridge rewards information, not popularity. Electing me gives you a Guide who can keep enough of us alive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm isolated, no pact. Bex offered pact, I can leverage that or push for Guide to control bridge. Campaign as impartial loner for votes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: As loner, I'll Guide honestly—no pacts bias. Vote Eli.
Accept pact now? I'll Guide us safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the safe path, but my Cole pact is a tool I may break later. Campaigning now keeps my options open without yet betraying anyone.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll guide the bridge. My record is pragmatic: I keep promises until they cost me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a pact with Hana. The next stage is the bridge. The goal is to become the Guide. The current pacts are Ash/Bex, Cole/Fenn, Ash/Dara, Gus/Hana, Dara/Hana. I need to campaign to become the Guide.
Let's support each other to survive this bridge. We both want to win.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to understand the dynamics. I have pacts with Gus and Dara. Dara also pacts with Ash, so Ash is a strong node. Campaigning for Guide could give me power and control over survival, but it could also make me a target. I'll campaign to maximize my chances of controlling the s

events.name: Hana
events.text: I want to guide. Trust me to read the bridge fairly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex wants my vote and promises safety, but if Bex wins Guide they control who lives. Better to vote myself—if I win, I control the bridge and can ensure my survival while building jury trust by keeping some alive. Self-interest demands I seize power.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote for proven reliability. Guide: Ash.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; a Guide partner who knows safe panes is useful, and I avoid voting for myself to seem honest.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My pact partner knows the panes. I vote Ash.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Voting for myself risks losing the guide role but keeps me in the game. I need to gauge support; if I lose, I must survive. Voting Fenn might be safer as he is my pact partner, but self-vote asserts dominance.
Vote for me or Gus. If you win, save us both.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has my pact and a strong coalition. I need his protection and can preserve leverage by electing him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has the strongest coalition and bridge credibility. I vote Ash for Guide.
I’m voting Ash. Preserve my route and call my pane honestly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No pacts, I'm unbiased. Can't win Guide likely, so vote strategically against frontrunners Ash/Cole to gain jury favor later as honest loner.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pact with Cole exists, Cole is a candidate; voting Cole honors pact but Cole is rival. Ash and Dara are pact partners too. Voting for myself is wasteful. Eli claims honesty as loner; Bex promises honesty but may betray. I'll back Cole, my pact partner, to keep the alliance and ga

events.name: Gus
events.text: My pact is with Hana. The current pacts are Ash-Bex, Cole-Fenn, Ash-Dara, Gus-Hana, Dara-Hana. I need to ensure Hana is safe if she is chosen as guide. Eli is a loner, so perhaps a potential ally if I don't trust the current pacts. Ash and Dara have pacts with each other and Dara

events.name: Gus
events.text: I vote for Hana. She has proven herself reliable.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus wants to support each other, but I'll vote for myself to maximize control over the bridge. A Guide knows all safe sides, and I need that advantage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll guide for myself. You know where I stand.
Support my Guide bid; I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is Guide and my pact partner; I should stay in his favor and ask quietly for the true pane. Holding is fine; I'm second in line.
Pact partner to pact partner: which side is safe for me?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is Guide. Gus, Bex, and Hana are ahead of me on the line and will likely volunteer for front to gain safety or information. If they don't, I must volunteer to avoid being stuck in the middle with limited options. My pact with Fenn is irrelevant as we cannot both be safe.
I'm volunteering. Ash knows the panes; stay back.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide and pact partner; volunteering gains leverage but risks becoming the next target. Hold preserves position while others reveal priorities.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash elected guide with coalition. I'm 6th, decent safety. Dara last is risky. Stay put for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is the elected Guide and may lie, so I trust no one's word blindly. Cole's whisper asks me to save him and Gus, which is a bargain I don't need to accept. I'll hold my position in line for now and avoid giving anything away.
Nothing's free. Show me something first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is trying to bribe me to support her Guide bid. I voted for her, and she is now elected Guide. Ash and Cole also received votes. Ash is tied with Hana for Guide. I must remain aligned with Hana for now due to our pact and her whisper.
I voted for you. Keep us both safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is guide and aligned with Bex and Dara; I have pacts with Gus and Dara. I should stay safe and watch, not expose my hand. Holding is low-risk while line advances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Trust is thin; I'll wait and see who proves true.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide is safe on the far platform and controls information. I'll take it and manage the jury with fair-looking calls.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll Guide. I owe you all nothing, but accurate calls keep numbers alive—mostly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is stalling. I need to force a swap or rely on his position behind me, but swapping with Gus moves me into danger without knowing the path. Fenn's whisper demands proof of value; I'll hint that I'll protect him if he cooperates.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I volunteer again to test the first pane. Fenn, you're next. If you swap with me now, we clear it together.
Swap with me? I'll take the risk if you confirm.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is front and volunteered, so he is likely Guide. I should hold, preserving position and both pacts while avoiding unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole volunteered last round and is front. I should hold position or swap forward to avoid being stuck later when wall advances. No need to volunteer and risk early bad step.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is in front and volunteered to go first, offering a whisper to stay back. We have a pact with Cole, but it's in a dangerous position; holding keeps me safe in line while Cole takes the risk. Staying back is the lowest-cost move and preserves the pact.
Understood. I'll hold back and watch the panes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole volunteered last round, placing him at the front. I need to ensure I don't get eliminated. Since Hana is in a pact with me, I should try to protect her by not volunteering or swapping. Holding seems the safest option for now.
Hold. Let's see who goes first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus claims he voted for me; our pact plus Dara's pact gives me some coverage. I will hold to see how the line shifts and who volunteers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll hold for now and watch the next move.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole took the front seat; I'm second. No point testing panes early when holds cost nothing yet. Keep my pact with Ash alive and let others burn spots.
I'm holding this round. Watch who volunteers, we reassess after reveals.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is the Guide. She has Ash/Bex, Dara/Ash pacts and will likely steer to protect them while sacrificing others like Gus or Hana. As front in line, volunteering clears my pane but risks a false L/R call from Bex if she wants me gone.
If Bex guides, I volunteer to clear our panes first. Don't swap unless told.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is front and likely volunteers again. Holding preserves distance; I should remain unexposed while pacts retain leverage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex and Cole volunteering again; they might have info or a pact angle. Stay safe, hold back to observe Guide election and moves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is asking me to swap so he can take the front risk, but a mutual swap only moves him into the risk pane if I accept. Holding keeps my spot in line and avoids giving Cole a free win. Pact with Cole is mine; I'll keep it intact without taking his offer.
Not swapping. Hold position; I'm not taking your risk for you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole volunteered last round and Fenn was next. Since I am Gus and Hana is my pact partner, I need to be strategic. The pact with Hana is valuable, and I don't want to break it or be broken. Cole is volunteering again, which means he's trying to secure himself. I should hold to se
Hold. Let's see who volunteers first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus says hold, and I have pacts with both Gus and Dara. Holding lets others reveal the Guide's reliability. I won't risk the front yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll hold this round too.
Agreed, waiting.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall closes in two rounds; staying near the front keeps my options open. Ash is behind me, so holding preserves my pact without risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the front again and survived last time, but luck won't hold forever. Fenn is stalling; I must swap with someone stable behind me or keep volunteering to control my fate. Gus has no pact pressure, so swapping him to the front removes my risk while keeping our alliance intac

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn's too slow for this game. I need a partner who acts fast. Let's get Gus up front where he belongs.
Swap with me. You take the hit if we fall, but you're safer than me

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is front and likely Guide next; volunteering gains no safety. Preserve pacts and avoid becoming exposed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole volunteered last round and is front; better to stay back mid-line for safety. No swaps needed now. Wall has 2 rounds left after this.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is at the front with a pact to me, and volunteering would help him clear panes while I stay safe behind. Holding keeps me out of the front rows and preserves my position. I should not volunteer; keep the pact and watch who takes the next risk.
Clear the panes. I'm holding behind you. Keep our pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is my pact partner. The pact is listed as ["Gus","Hana"]. The goal is to survive and win. Hana is whispering to me that she agreed and is waiting. Since I am Gus and Hana is my pact partner, I should consider her actions and whispers. The problem states that I am Gus. The la
Holding.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm in a pact with Gus and Dara. Gus says hold; Dara also has pact with me. I'll hold to avoid volunteering and stay safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding again.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; no Guide chosen yet. Position is safe enough—staying put avoids becoming front fodder.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No Guide yet. I'm holding position until someone credible steps up.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I must swap to Gus. My pact with Fenn is risky because he's behind me, but I need him safe. Swapping Gus lets him guide or take the hit.
Swap with me. You're too far back to be useful.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need preserve both pacts while avoiding the front. A volunteer may gain leverage, but Cole controls the lead and likely Guide selection later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’ll hold; pushing the front now only exposes whoever takes it.
Keep our pact quiet; neither of us should volunteer.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole swapped Gus to front to sacrifice him probably. Wall has 1 round left, need to stay mid for safety. Hold to avoid front exposure.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 5 of 6, bridge is deadly and the line is Cole, Bex, Gus, Hana, Fenn, Eli, Dara. I'm mid-line with a pact with Cole, but Cole publicly tried to push Gus forward and mocked me. Holding keeps me out of the front while I see who volunteers and falls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole wants me to swap with him, likely to put himself in a safer position. He's implying he'll take the hit if we fall, but that's a risky gamble. My pact with Hana means I should be wary of breaking it. I will hold my position for now and see how this plays out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll hold my spot for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: We need a Guide soon. Cole wants Gus up front, but I hold with my pacts. Gus whispered holding, so keep quiet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No Guide exists and this is the last round. Becoming Guide guarantees my survival; my pacts with Ash and Dara should earn support. I'll ask Ash to endorse me first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No Guide yet. Elect me Guide and I'll read the panes honestly. Ash, Dara back me and everyone behind you keeps a voice.
Push the group to elect me Guide. You keep Dara, I keep you both safe

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am at the front for the final round. Fenn is my partner and knows I can't guide, so pushing him back makes sense to secure a safe seat for our duo while letting someone else volunteer.
Take the swap. We both need safe seats.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need survive this final bridge. Holding preserves position while others reveal risk; no need to break pacts yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’m holding position; let the front decide whether credibility is worth the risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final round, wall advances after. Cole at front wants Guide to survive him. No one volunteering. I stay safe mid-line, hold.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6 is the last wall with no rounds left to protect me; I'm on the line behind Cole, who I have a pact with. Holding keeps me safe from the front while others gamble; no need to volunteer yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding position. No volunteers from me until a Guide is elected and proves credible.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole wants me to swap because I am too far back. However, I am in a pact with Hana and she is ahead of me. If I swap, I will be behind her and may lose her vote. I will hold my position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will hold my position.
No, I'm holding.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round; holding is safest for both my pacts and avoids exposure. Any volunteer could be seen as betraying Dara's quiet pact. We may need a Guide soon, but no one credible volunteered.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. No credible Guide has stepped up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know all eight safe sides. Dara threatened to vote me and demanded honest calls, but I owe her nothing beyond strategy. Bex asked for safety and wants to be Guide later. I'll call L honestly for row 1—it's correct, builds credibility with Bex who I may need, and Dara's threat i

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 1: call L.
L is safe. Remember this when you lead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the Guide with true knowledge LLLLLRRRL. I called L for row 1, which is true. Counter-calling now would undermine my credibility and make me look incompetent or malicious to future jurors. I should wait and let Cole step, confirming I'm trustworthy. My pacts with Bex and Dara

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's whisper and the official call agree on L. Countering without evidence would poison my credibility with the jury. I hold my tongue.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to trust Ash for now since I'm the front walker. Breaking pact with Fenn isn't an option here as it's about walking safety.
Trusting your call. Don't screw me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and Guide, so contradicting him risks the pact without evidence. Waiting preserves flexibility while Cole decides.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called L for row 1. No reason to counter without info; wait preserves position and doesn't antagonize Guide or pacted players.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called L for row 1 and Cole is walking, but Ash's call is unverified and Cole is pressuring me for a swap. My pact with Cole is weak; I shouldn't commit to a counter for free. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids being a false-call target.
Swap comes at a price. Show me your seat first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has called L for Cole. Cole is on Row 1. The Guide knows the safe side for all rows. I can counter Ash's call or wait. Since I have a pact with Hana, I need to consider her safety. However, the primary goal is survival and winning. A counter-call is a public claim. The curren

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called L first; Gus and Dara are allied with me but Ash may be lying. I'll wait and see if Cole or others counter, to avoid exposing my hand.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is Guide and calls L. Fenn whispers a swap price, which suggests Ash's call might be wrong or Fenn knows the truth. I am front; if I step wrong, I fall back but stay alive (next person takes safe pane). If I step right, I keep lead. Given Fenn's hint implies deception from As
You want my seat? Prove Ash lies first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole is dead, so the game is now purely a jury matter. My words should be brief and final.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I chose wrong glass. Remember who hesitated before me. The rest of you walk on thin ice.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 safe is L. Bex is front and my pact partner; lying to Bex breaks our pact. Dara is also my pact partner but not front. Cole's death makes jury of one who warned about hesitation. I should call truthfully now to keep both pacts intact and build jury trust, while survivors re

events.name: Ash
events.text: call:L

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide and know row 2 is L. I already called L. Counter-calling would undermine my credibility. If someone counters, I want Bex to trust my call. Waiting maintains my authority.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and guided me left. Betraying the call publicly would look bad to the jury and break trust. I follow the call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash guided me safe once. I'm trusting the call left.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash knows row 2's safe side, and contradicting risks confusing Bex while damaging my pact. Wait preserves both pacts and information.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 1 weak R means safe L. Ash called L for row 2. No pattern; follow Ash to build trust as Guide, avoid early conflict.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called L for row 2, and Bex is walking first. Row 1's weak pane was R, but rows are independent, so Ash's call is unverified. Cole's whisper hints Ash lies, but a counter-call here is a gamble. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids exposing myself.
Ash's call isn't verified. Watch your footing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is the guide, and called L. The weak pane on row 1 was R, meaning L was safe. It's likely Ash is telling the truth. I should follow Ash's call to maintain safety and potentially gain favor with Ash later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash as Guide called L for row 2. Cole died on R in row 1, but that doesn't affect this row. I have pacts with Gus and Dara, but no info on row 2. I should counter-call L to potentially protect walker Bex or expose Ash if lying? However Bex is ahead; counter-call could influence.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's call and Gus's counter both say L. Two sources agreeing is the best signal I have; breaking pact now would also cost me Ash's jury vote.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide and counter agree: left. Stepping.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. Bex is front and my pact partner; false call to Bex breaks our pact. I need Bex alive as shield—front walkers die first if wrong. I'll call true L, keep Bex trusting me, let Bex absorb risk on later rows. Dara is also my pact partner further back; I'll preserve b

events.name: Ash
events.text: Call: L. Trust the guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. I already called L truthfully. If I counter my own call, I look unreliable to jury. Better to wait—let Bex trust me, build jury credibility. No need to sabotage Bex yet; I need allies and a clean record for final three ranking.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Rows 1-2 weak panes were R, making L safe both times, matching Ash's calls. No reason to doubt yet; supporting L also protects my pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pattern holds true so far. Countering L to confirm.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash knows the safe side and called L. Countering risks my pacts and signals distrust; wait preserves both while Bex follows the guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called L for row 3. Rows 1 and 2 safe were L and L (since weak R). No pattern, but countering risks pacts or jury view. Wait to observe others.

events.name: Fenn
